title: Institutional vs ad-hoc arbitration - what clients should actually choose
p1: Many clients choose arbitration thinking it automatically means faster justice. But the real question is not arbitration vs court. It is: who will manage the process when things get complicated?
p2: A common misconception is that institutional arbitration is always expensive and ad-hoc arbitration is always cheaper. The reality is different. In ad-hoc arbitration, parties manage everything themselves — from appointing arbitrators to setting procedures. This can save costs, but disagreements about the process can create delays.
p3: Institutional arbitration involves an established body that provides rules, administrative support, and a framework for handling disputes. This can be valuable in high-value or complex matters where structure matters more than saving every rupee. Smaller, straightforward disputes with cooperative parties may work well with ad-hoc arbitration. The right choice depends on risk, complexity, and the willingness of parties to cooperate.
conclusion: If you were drafting an arbitration clause today, would you prefer the flexibility of ad-hoc arbitration or the structured support of institutional arbitration?
